requirements.title: Honest QR copy: labels need the TracePoint app
requirements.requirement: The QR modal, printed label and Help article state plainly that a printed label opens only in the TracePoint mobile app, instead of 'Scan with a mobile device to open this vehicle'. 'Copy Link' no longer implies a usable web link.
acceptance: Component test: the viewOnly and full QR modals render text naming the TracePoint app (e.g. 'Scan with the TracePoint mobile app') and no longer render 'Scan with a mobile device to open this vehicle'.
'Copy Link' is renamed (e.g. 'Copy app code') or copies an HTTPS URL if MOD-FLT-002 adopts one.
The Help 'Manage fleet vehicles' article mentions QR scanning and that it needs the app.
QR payload produced by buildTracePointQrValue is unchanged unless MOD-FLT-002 is decided.
requirements.notes: D-49 (Help said 'Coming soon') was fixed in the RC; only the missing QR/app mention remains. Web copy only; the scan path itself is owned by FLT-04/ARM-01.

requirements.title: Decide and build a web/HTTPS fallback for QR labels
requirements.requirement: Agencies without the native app can open a printed vehicle or equipment label: labels (or a second QR) carry an HTTPS deep link that lands on the vehicle inspection / equipment record after sign-in, and the resolver accepts the HTTPS form.
acceptance: Owner decision recorded on the URL scheme and the native-client contract before implementation.
Unit test: parseTracePointQrValue round-trips the HTTPS form as well as tracepoint:// labels already printed.
Scanning an HTTPS label with a stock phone camera opens the record after sign-in (deep link preserved through login).
Uniform not-found response for absent and unauthorized items is preserved (B5/F4 behaviour).
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: whether QR labels should support web-only users (HTTPS form) or remain native-only with honest web copy (remediation plan §8 item 10, D-01/FLT-04).

requirements.title: QR resolver accepts printed labels, unit numbers and serials
requirements.requirement: The QR resolver and custody lookup resolve the printed tracepoint://kind/id value, bare UUIDs, unit numbers, asset numbers and serials without 400/500, and vehicle scans are not denied by a nonexistent feature flag.
acceptance: Unit number, asset number, serial and the printed label all resolve (staging step S4).
A non-UUID identifier on PostgreSQL never returns 500.
A non-member gets the same response for absent and denied items.
requirements.notes: Batches B5 (QR resolve), F5 (NEW-F5-A vehicle scans denied), F6b (QR decisions) and F4 (disclosure), merged into the integration branch. Not validated on staging. Shared with Armory ARM-01 / NEW-ARM-B. Web scan path remains absent (MOD-FLT-002).

requirements.title: Fleet managers can print vehicle QR labels from the vehicle record
requirements.requirement: Users who can manage fleet get the full QR label (Print and Download PNG) on the vehicle record header; other users keep the view-only label.
acceptance: Component test: a manager sees Print/Download on the vehicle record; a non-manager sees the view-only label.
The UI only hides or disables controls; the server stays the authority for permissions and no permission logic moves into components (blueprint §1b).
The QR payload and the label print layout are unchanged.

requirements.title: Vehicle inspection items start 'Not inspected' with explicit 'Mark remaining as Pass'
requirements.requirement: Every vehicle checklist item starts unanswered ('Not inspected'); only a condition an equipment record already shows is carried in. An explicit 'Mark remaining N as Pass' fills only unanswered, non-critical items, and an unanswered item is never sent. The 'Mark only what changed' / 'Ready for one-tap submission' copy is gone.
acceptance: Every checklist item starts unanswered; nothing is pre-set to Pass, and Submit stays disabled and lists what is missing until required items are answered (blueprint §1b).
'Mark remaining as Pass' never covers the vehicle's critical items; they must be answered individually (blueprint §1b).
fleet/inspection-form.test.ts and InspectionChoiceControl.test.tsx pass; staging step S27 shows checks start Not inspected.
No unanswered item appears in the POST payload.
requirements.notes: UX-RB-2 (owner decision 2026-10-22: checklists default to 'Not inspected' with an optional explicit 'Mark remaining as Pass'). Not merged into ec027f50; not deployed or validated on staging. Verify that critical items are excluded from 'Mark remaining' per §1b when the Checklist component (MOD-FLT-012) is built.

requirements.title: Inspection API refuses items without an explicit condition
requirements.requirement: The inspection route no longer records an item with a missing or unknown condition as Pass; it returns 400 instead, so neither web nor native clients can create a pre-passed record.
acceptance: Route test: a checklist item without Pass/Defect/Critical is refused with 400 and nothing is written.
Native contract row (proposed C33) added and the native client confirmed compatible before release.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: UX-RB flagged the server-side default Pass but did not change it because /api/mobile re-exports the route; returning 400 needs an owner decision and contract row C33.

requirements.title: Inspection odometer starts empty with a 'Last: N' hint
requirements.requirement: The inspection mileage and hours fields start empty and show the last known reading as a hint, so a stale value is not stored as the reading; entry is required (or an unchanged value is warned about) per the agency decision.
acceptance: Component test: the mileage field starts empty and shows 'Last: N'.
Submit requires a reading (or warns when it equals the last value), per the decision.
Route test: the stored inspection mileage equals the submitted value.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: FLT-10 balance (require fresh odometer entry vs warn), decided together with the checklist default.

requirements.title: Record inspection elapsed time and device; flag very fast inspections
requirements.requirement: Inspections record elapsed time and device, and inspections completed in under an agency-set threshold are flagged for review.
acceptance: Route test: elapsed time and device are stored with the inspection.
An inspection under the threshold is flagged in history; the flag never blocks the save.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: FLT-10 is 'Enhancement – defer'; agency policy decides whether and how fast inspections are flagged.

requirements.title: Inspection outcome message reflects real readiness, hold and audit status
requirements.requirement: After submit, the message is built from the server's readiness status, safetyHold, work order and audit result: a held or Out of Service vehicle is reported as 'Out of Service. Do not use it.' with the hold reason; unknown readiness never claims ready; audit pending/unrecorded is shown as a warning; a 500 that carries the inspection closes the form and says not to resubmit.
acceptance: fleet/inspection-outcome.test.ts covers held without work order, open critical work order, attention, available, audit pending/unrecorded, 500 with inspection, and missing readiness.
Staging step S27: with 'defect creates work order' off, a critical defect shows 'Out of Service. Do not use it.' and the vehicle is Out of Service.
Saved / not saved status is shown only from the server response, never optimistically (blueprint §1b).
requirements.notes: UX-RB-3 on claude/fix-uxrb-release-safety; not merged into ec027f50, not deployed or validated.

requirements.title: Inspection, work order and status writes are atomic; audit failure never hides a defect
requirements.requirement: A failed work-order insert can no longer silently drop a critical defect: the inspection, work order and status refresh succeed or fail together (audit delivered through the outbox), and a critical inspection whose work order failed holds the vehicle Out of Service.
acceptance: Fleet handler tests: a failed work order rolls back or holds the vehicle; the audit outbox delivers the inspection audit (fleet-audit-outbox-native tests).
Response includes readiness and audit status consumed by MOD-FLT-009.
requirements.notes: Batch B4 (fleet integrity, audit outbox 043) with F3/F6a safety hold (046). Owner to confirm B4 outbox deviations 1–4. Not validated on staging.

requirements.title: Idempotency key for inspection and evidence submissions (offline replay safe)
requirements.requirement: Inspection and inspection-evidence POSTs accept a client operation/idempotency key so a resubmission or offline replay cannot create duplicate inspections or work orders.
acceptance: Route test: two POSTs with the same key create one inspection and one work order.
Native contract row added; requests without a key behave as today.
requirements.notes: FLT-17 offline queueing/draft persistence belongs to the native client (status 'Verify'); this requirement covers the confirmed server gap. Web draft persistence is optional and not separately required.

requirements.title: Field-grade vehicle Checklist (44px segmented control, sticky result and Submit)

sources.ref: Inspection checklist as a compact table

requirements.requirement: The vehicle inspection uses the shared Checklist: Pass / Defect / N/A as ≥44px segments with no default, a note and 'Can it be driven?' only on a defect, a progress count, and a sticky footer showing the result and its status effect ('goes out of service') with Submit as the only primary action. Text is never under 12px.
acceptance: Every checklist item starts unanswered; nothing is pre-set to Pass, and Submit stays disabled and lists what is missing until required items are answered (blueprint §1b).
Safety-critical items cannot be bulk-filled; the result and status effect are shown before Submit (blueprint §1b).
At 375px, every condition target is ≥44×44px and no inspection text is under 12px (axe + measurement).
Same inspection payload as UX-RB-2 (network-log comparison); Network-log comparison shows the same endpoints and payloads as the baseline, and no audit-log difference (blueprint §4 feature parity).
requirements.notes: Blueprint §4 lists the checklist redesign for R2 'built on UX-RB-2 behaviour'; §5 places it in Stage 3. Must not fork UX-RB-2.

requirements.title: Quick Inspect opens the form directly; vehicle tabs honour ?tab=
requirements.requirement: One 'Inspect vehicle' action opens the checklist directly (no second 'Start Inspection'), and the vehicle record reads ?tab= (and an inspect flag) so alert links such as ?tab=maintenance land on the right tab; inventory filters move to a separate parameter so the back link still works.
acceptance: Component test: /fleet-management/<id>?tab=maintenance opens Maintenance; ?tab=inspections&start=1 opens the form.
Fleet notification links (fleet-notifications.ts) land on their tab.
Old URLs keep working; the back link returns to the filtered list.

requirements.title: Vehicle GET returns canInspect / canReportIssue
requirements.requirement: The vehicle GET returns canInspect from canSubmitFleetInspection and the equivalent issue-reporting eligibility, so clients can tell a user before they fill a form that the server will refuse it.
acceptance: Route test: an unlisted view_fleet user gets canInspect=false; an eligible user gets true.
Native contract row added before implementation (field is additive on a re-exported route).
The server still enforces eligibility on POST (no change).
requirements.notes: UX-RB §5: 'D-R1 adds a field to a route the native app re-exports, so it needs a contract row before implementation.'

requirements.title: Hide or disable Inspect and Report Issue for ineligible users
requirements.requirement: Inspect and Report Issue are hidden or disabled with an explanation when the vehicle payload says the user is not eligible, so nobody completes a whole checklist only to get 403.
acceptance: Component test: canInspect=false disables Inspect with a reason; true shows it.
The UI only hides or disables controls; the server stays the authority for permissions and no permission logic moves into components (blueprint §1b).
requirements.notes: Blocked on the backend field (MOD-FLT-014) and its native contract row.

requirements.title: Web photo capture for inspection defects and issue reports
requirements.requirement: Web users can add a photo to a defect and to an issue report (camera capture on phones), uploaded to the existing evidence route after the inspection is created, and it appears in History.
acceptance: Component and route test: an upload posts to the existing evidence route and appears in History.
Upload failure is shown in place; the saved inspection is not resubmitted.
Uses the shared EvidenceCapture pattern (QuickQualificationCamera).
requirements.notes: OA classifies FLT-03 as 'Defer (missing capability)'; remediation plan puts web evidence in Phase 2. Native capture requires runtime verification.

requirements.title: Evidence API validates checklist item and supports a mandatory-photo rule
requirements.requirement: The evidence route rejects a checklistItemId that is not on the inspection, writes its audit atomically with the upload, and supports a configurable rule requiring a photo for Damage and Critical defects.
acceptance: Route test: an unknown checklist item returns 400 (T9 no longer reproduces).
With the rule on, a Critical defect without a photo is reported as incomplete per the decided behaviour.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: whether a photo becomes mandatory for Critical/Damage defects (FLT-03 correction says configurable).

requirements.title: Evidence thumbnails open a viewer instead of downloading
requirements.requirement: Tapping an evidence card opens it in a viewer (lightbox via viewUrl) rather than downloading the file.
acceptance: Component test: tapping a thumbnail opens a viewer; download remains available as a secondary action.

requirements.title: Inspection history shows failed items and defect notes
requirements.requirement: Each inspection in History expands its non-Pass items with label, condition and note.
acceptance: Component test: an inspection with a Critical item renders the item label and its note.

requirements.title: Vehicle list returns safety hold, last inspection result and open work
requirements.requirement: The fleet list response includes each vehicle's safety-hold state, last inspection result and date, and open work-order count, so the list can be filtered without per-vehicle requests.
acceptance: Route test: a held vehicle's list row carries safetyHold; a vehicle whose last inspection failed carries that result.
Response stays additive; existing fields unchanged.

requirements.title: Fleet manager triage: Safety hold / Failed inspection / Open work filters and badges
requirements.requirement: The fleet list shows a Safety hold badge on held vehicles and offers 'Safety hold', 'Last inspection failed' and 'Open work' filters (URL-synced), with KPI numbers linking to the filtered list.
acceptance: Component test: a held vehicle shows the hold badge in its row/card; the Safety hold filter lists only held vehicles.
Filters are in the URL and survive reload.
requirements.notes: Blocked on the list API fields (MOD-FLT-020).

requirements.title: Safety hold visible on the vehicle header; status buttons disabled while held
requirements.requirement: A held vehicle shows a 'Safety hold' chip in the record header with source and since-date. While held, Available and Attention are disabled with 'Clear the safety hold first', so a manager is never told 'Saved' for a status that did not change.
acceptance: Component test: with safetyHold present, the header shows the hold and Available/Attention are disabled with the explanation.

Clearing the hold still requires the existing reason and writes the same audit entry; Reason fields stay required where they are today, and the same audit entry (actor, time, reason, before and after) is still written (blueprint §1b).
requirements.notes: Listed by UX-RB §5 as a 'before production promotion' item not yet done.

requirements.title: Server refuses a status change that a safety hold would override
requirements.requirement: A PATCH to Available or Attention on a held vehicle returns 409 and does not set status_override_active, instead of 200 with the status silently re-escalated.
acceptance: Route test: PATCH status=Available on a held vehicle returns 409 and leaves the override flag unchanged.

requirements.title: Manual override semantics after a safety hold is released
requirements.requirement: Once a hold is released by a clean inspection or a clearance, the vehicle's status follows the decided override semantics instead of staying Out of Service indefinitely because an override flag was left active.
acceptance: Staging step S12 runtime check performed first.
Route test (held, override, clean inspection) gives the decided status.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: whether a safety hold should clear a manual status override (remediation plan §8 item 12). Fails safe today.

requirements.title: List status is read-only; status changes go through the record
requirements.requirement: The inline status <select> and prompt are removed from list rows; the row shows a status chip and status changes happen through 'Change status…' on the record.
acceptance: Component test: the list has no status <select>.

Status changes still require a reason and write the same audit; Reason fields stay required where they are today, and the same audit entry (actor, time, reason, before and after) is still written (blueprint §1b).
requirements.notes: Blueprint §4 keeps the status change flow unchanged in R1; this lands with the StatusChangeSheet (Stage 3).

requirements.title: StatusChangeSheet / ReasonDialog replaces native prompts (status, hold clearance, mileage correction)
requirements.screen: /fleet-management/[vehicleId] Manage Status; Clear Safety Hold; vehicle form mileage correction
requirements.requirement: Vehicle status changes and Clear Safety Hold open a sheet with a required reason, a before → after summary, an audit notice and a submit button naming the effect; one-tap coloured status pills and window.prompt are removed. Cancelling or an empty reason shows a message instead of silently aborting.
acceptance: Reason fields stay required where they are today, and the same audit entry (actor, time, reason, before and after) is still written (blueprint §1b).

Destructive or broad-impact actions use a ConfirmDialog naming the record and impact; accountable state changes use a sheet with a required reason and an audit notice, with no extra 'Are you sure?' (blueprint §1b).
No window.prompt remains in the fleet pages (grep).

Same PATCH endpoints and payloads (reason included) as the baseline; Network-log comparison shows the same endpoints and payloads as the baseline, and no audit-log difference (blueprint §4 feature parity).

requirements.title: Vehicle add/edit modal: in-modal errors, in-modal correction reason, sectioned form
requirements.requirement: Validation and save errors render inside the vehicle modal footer; lowering mileage shows an in-modal 'correction reason' field beside Save instead of a window.prompt; the ~26 fields are grouped into sections with a sticky footer.
acceptance: Component test: a 400 from PATCH renders inside the modal.
Lowering mileage shows the required reason field; cancelling shows a message, never a silent abort.
The footer stays visible while scrolling.
Reason fields stay required where they are today, and the same audit entry (actor, time, reason, before and after) is still written (blueprint §1b).

requirements.title: Fleet dialogs: Escape, focus trap, initial focus
requirements.screen: FleetWorkOrderDialog, FleetEquipmentDialog, vehicle modal, QR modal
requirements.requirement: All fleet dialogs close on Escape, trap focus, set initial focus and return focus to the trigger.
acceptance: Component and axe test per dialog: Esc closes, focus is trapped and returns to the trigger; no new axe violations.

requirements.title: Remove the editable 'Open Issues' field
requirements.requirement: The vehicle form no longer offers an editable Open Issues count; the count is shown read-only from the server.
acceptance: Component test: the field is absent from the form; the list still shows the computed count.

requirements.title: Server ignores client openIssueCount on vehicle create and edit
requirements.requirement: Vehicle POST and PATCH ignore openIssueCount; the count is always derived from open work orders, including on create.
acceptance: Route test: POST with openIssueCount: 5 stores 0 (or the real count); PATCH cannot change it.
requirements.notes: B4 fixed FLT-19 only partially ('field remains'); register-D shows a typed count still persists on create (api/fleet/vehicles/route.ts:188).

requirements.title: Consolidate the two vehicle PATCH endpoints
requirements.requirement: Both vehicle PATCH paths go through one service function with the same status validation, monotonic mileage rule, audit and readiness refresh.
acceptance: Route tests: an invalid status returns 400 on both paths; both refresh readiness; both audit identically.
requirements.notes: B4 aligned FLT-20 partially (remediation-status: 'FLT-19/20 (partial)'). Remaining scope to be confirmed against the integration branch.

requirements.title: A manual status override never masks a critical defect
requirements.requirement: Manual overrides can only escalate; a critical inspection defect after any manual status change still puts the vehicle Out of Service, and critical safety holds always apply.
acceptance: Fleet handler test T1b no longer reproduces: PATCH Available, then a Critical defect, gives Out of Service (staging step S2).
requirements.notes: Batches B4 (overrides escalate only) and F3/F6a (safety hold, 046 status guard). Not validated on staging. UI consequences are MOD-FLT-022, MOD-FLT-023 and MOD-FLT-024.

requirements.title: Odometer only moves forward; blank is not zero; corrections need a reason
requirements.screen: Work-order, issue, inspection and vehicle PATCH routes
requirements.requirement: No write path lowers current_mileage except an explicit odometer correction with a reason and audit; empty or null mileage means 'not provided', never 0.
acceptance: Fleet handler tests T2, T3 and T4 no longer reproduce.
A correction without a reason is refused and the audit records before/after.
requirements.notes: Batch B4. The FLT-09 upper sanity bound on large jumps is not confirmed in the batch notes; verify. UI for the correction reason is MOD-FLT-027.

requirements.title: Issue report: no operability default; 'Limited use' wired or removed
requirements.requirement: The operability question starts with no selection and Submit is blocked until a choice is made; 'Limited use / needs review' either maps to Attention with a review flag or is removed, so it is never recorded the same as 'Safe to operate'.
acceptance: Component test: Submit shows 'choose operability' when nothing is selected.
Route/component test: each operability choice maps to the expected affects_availability and readiness.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: remove 'Limited use' or wire it to Attention plus a review flag (D-09 / FLT-13). Wiring it needs a backend change.

requirements.title: Shorter issue reporting: one drivability question, mileage carried over
requirements.requirement: Issue reporting asks what's wrong and 'Can it be driven?' (priority derived from the answer), carries mileage from the last reading, and the submit label names whoever owns fleet repairs instead of 'Submit to Mechanic' when no mechanic role exists.
acceptance: Officer path drops from ~12 to ~6 clicks (walkthrough recorded).

Same work-order POST payload semantics as the baseline (priority and affectsAvailability still sent); Network-log comparison shows the same endpoints and payloads as the baseline, and no audit-log difference (blueprint §4 feature parity).

requirements.title: Vehicle damage / collision record with supervisor review
requirements.requirement: A 'Vehicle damage / collision' record type captures incident date/time, location, other party, injuries, report number, photos and a required supervisor acknowledgement.
acceptance: Route and UI tests: a damage record cannot be closed without supervisor acknowledgement; it links to the incident number.
requirements.notes: OA: Enhancement – defer.

requirements.title: Repeat inspection defects append to the open work order
requirements.requirement: Defects are keyed by vehicle and checklist item; a defect already on an open work order adds an 'observed again' note instead of a new work order, and the checklist shows 'known open defect (WO #)'.
acceptance: Route test T7: three identical defective inspections produce one work order with two 'observed again' notes.
requirements.notes: OA: Defer (missing capability).

requirements.title: Fleet alerts generated without the recipient opening the app
requirements.requirement: Critical defects, out-of-service transitions and due dates create notifications for fleet managers and mechanics on a schedule (and ideally on write), honouring notify_by_email and escalation_hours, so a phone-only manager sees them in the inbox.
acceptance: Staging: a critical defect creates an inbox item and email for a fleet manager who has not opened the web app.
requirements.notes: B6 adds scheduled per-department generation (TRN-01/FLT-05) but is kept out of the integration pending the infrastructure decision. Write-time enqueue is not in B6. Overlaps the platform notification work.

requirements.title: Fleet rule settings are enforced or removed
requirements.requirement: Each fleet rule (require_return_to_service_approval, default_service_*, *_warning_days, escalation_hours, notify_by_email, fleet_manager_role_codes) is either implemented server-side or removed from the rules API.
acceptance: Per decided rule: a handler test proves the rule changes behaviour, or the field is gone from GET/PUT.
requirements.notes: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: FLT-06 'Fix – owner decision on intended behavior' (implement vs hide each inert setting; return-to-service approval would also need the approvals queue).

requirements.title: Fleet Rules: inert or always-on settings shown honestly
requirements.requirement: Settings that are not enforced are hidden or labelled 'Not yet active', and 'Critical issues remove vehicles from service' is a locked 'Always on' row; the remaining automation toggle states exactly what it governs.
acceptance: Component test: no inert setting renders as a live switch; the critical rule renders as locked 'Always on'.

Stored rule values and the PUT payload are unchanged except for removed controls; Network-log comparison shows the same endpoints and payloads as the baseline, and no audit-log difference (blueprint §4 feature parity).
requirements.notes: E-61 comes from UX appendix E (Admin group); kept here because it is the Fleet Rules panel.

requirements.title: Fleet Rules role lists: commas typeable, role picker
requirements.requirement: Role-code and other comma lists can be typed key by key (parse on blur or chip input), and inspection/routing roles are chosen from a multi-select fed by department roles, so a typo cannot make every officer ineligible to inspect.
acceptance: Component test: typing 'officer, sergeant' key by key sends both codes in the PUT body.
The role picker lists only existing department roles.
requirements.notes: UX-RB §5 lists D-27 as not done. Impact raised by F2 (inspection_role_codes now excludes unlisted members).

requirements.title: Fleet Rules cannot save defaults after a failed load
requirements.requirement: A failed rules GET shows an explicit error with Try again, and Save is unavailable until the real rules load, so defaults can never overwrite agency policy.
acceptance: FleetRulesPanel.test.tsx: HTTP 500 → error, no Save, no PUT; retry loads.
requirements.notes: Fixed in UX-RB2-2 (commit 8bfbab2) per register-SV SV-30; branch not named in the sources. SV-30 is live evidence of the defect on staging 22e543d, not of the fix.

requirements.title: Fleet Rules: sticky SaveBar, unsaved-changes guard, confirm template removal
requirements.requirement: Fleet Rules has a sticky SaveBar showing dirty state, warns on navigating away with unsaved changes, and checklist-template Remove asks for confirmation.
acceptance: Component test: Remove asks for confirmation; navigating away while dirty warns.

Destructive or broad-impact actions use a ConfirmDialog naming the record and impact; accountable state changes use a sheet with a required reason and an audit notice, with no extra 'Are you sure?' (blueprint §1b).

requirements.title: Fleet Rules checklist template uses the dark theme
requirements.requirement: The checklist template section uses the dark token palette instead of a light-theme island.
acceptance: Visual regression at 1280/768/375 shows no light-theme surfaces in the panel.

requirements.title: One location for Fleet Rules
requirements.screen: /settings/fleet vs Settings > Rules > Fleet; vehicle header gear
requirements.requirement: Fleet rules live in one Settings location; the other entry becomes a 'Manage' link, and the standalone back link returns to the right place.
acceptance: Old /settings/fleet URL redirects to the single location; the vehicle gear links there.
requirements.notes: E-08 (Settings tab not in URL) belongs to the settings module; only the fleet duplicate is here.

requirements.title: Fleet list as DataTable with phone CardList and record drawer
requirements.requirement: The fleet list fits 1280px with Unit, Vehicle, Assigned, Status, Next due and Issues (unit and plate in mono); the row is the link and opens a drawer with reason and work order plus 'Open record'; below 640px rows render as cards; filters collapse to one 'Filters (n)' button below 768px; dark scrollbars.
acceptance: Visual regression at 1280, 768 and 375 (loaded, empty, loading, error, many rows).
No horizontal scroll at 1280px; at 375px each card shows unit, plate, status, next due and issues.
Existing filters, sorts and URL parameters keep working; Network-log comparison shows the same endpoints and payloads as the baseline, and no audit-log difference (blueprint §4 feature parity).
Verified with Officer, Fleet Manager, Supervisor and Admin accounts: what each role can see and do matches the baseline (blueprint §4).
requirements.notes: R1 representative screen. The status change flow is unchanged in R1.

requirements.title: Fleet KPI strip: neutral at zero, every number linked
requirements.requirement: Fleet summary tiles use the shared KpiTile: neutral at zero, coloured only when attention is needed, each linking to the filtered list.
acceptance: Visual regression shows no coloured zero tiles; each tile links to its filtered list.

requirements.title: Vehicle record header: one primary 'Inspect vehicle', labelled icon buttons, flattened overview
requirements.requirement: The vehicle record keeps its header pattern but has one primary action (Inspect vehicle), secondary/quiet buttons instead of green/amber/blue fills, aria-labels on the gear and refresh icon buttons, and overview fields as a definition list instead of one bordered tile each.
acceptance: axe: the icon buttons have accessible names.
Visual regression: exactly one primary button in the header.

requirements.title: Vehicle load failure: Back, Retry and access message
requirements.requirement: A failed vehicle load shows Back, Retry, and a plain explanation for 403 versus not found, which matters for QR and native-app arrivals.
acceptance: Component test: 403 shows the access message with Back; a network error shows Retry.

requirements.title: Preview vehicle and 'migration' copy only behind a dev flag
requirements.requirement: The fake PREVIEW_VEHICLE and 'Local preview mode' copy appear only with a development flag; otherwise a 'migration not applied' error shows a real error state.
acceptance: Component test: with the flag off, a 'migration' error shows the error state and no vehicle row.

requirements.title: Fleet copy and labels: no jargon, raw codes or stale claims
requirements.screen: /fleet-management list subtitle; vehicle Maintenance and History tabs
requirements.requirement: The list subtitle reads e.g. 'Status updates automatically from inspections and repairs' instead of 'Current status is authoritative…'; 'Hybrid readiness' is removed; raw role codes and action enums in Maintenance and History display as labels.
acceptance: No 'authoritative' or 'hybrid readiness' text in fleet pages (grep).
History and Maintenance render mapped labels; component test with a raw enum input shows its label.

requirements.title: One message region on the vehicle record
requirements.requirement: Page and inspection banners no longer stack and persist; completed actions use a toast and errors stay where the action was taken.
acceptance: Component test: two successive actions show one current message.

requirements.title: 12px type floor on fleet screens
requirements.requirement: No fleet text renders under 12px; labels are sentence case at 13px.
acceptance: Automated scan of fleet pages finds no computed font-size under 12px.

requirements.title: Vehicle equipment: one source of truth with Equipment, with edit and remove
requirements.requirement: Linking equipment to a vehicle sets equipment_assets.assigned_vehicle_id in the same transaction, Fleet reads vehicle equipment from it, PATCH and remove (with reason) exist, and fleet managers can read unassigned and vehicle-assigned assets for the picker.
acceptance: Route test: linking in Fleet sets assigned_vehicle_id; custody then refuses a personal check-out of that asset.
Remove requires a reason and writes an audit entry.
requirements.notes: OA: Defer (missing capability).

requirements.title: Vehicle Equipment tab: edit/remove, 'Unit' naming, inventory on the vehicle
